newsitem.title: UK: Further expansion crucial- Berisford chief.
newsitem.headline: Further expansion crucial- Berisford chief.

text.p: Consumer food equipment to agribusiness manufacturer Berisford Plc said on Friday it would not consider any possible bid offer for the company unless it fitted into its future expansion plans.
"I am committed to taking the company forward, the expansion. I have not requested an offer, it has come," Alan Bowkett, chief executive of Berisford, told Reuters in a telephone conversation.
Bowkett said Berisford's Welbilt unit in the United States was expanding in Latin American and Far East markets and he would ensure that these plans went ahead.
"I have to see that it (expansion) goes forward. These are real matters," Bowkett said.

The company said on Friday it had received a "formal interest" in an offer from a potential bidder. Its share price rose to 151 pence at 1500 GMT from Thursday's close of 121 p in a trade volume of more than 2.85 million shares.
Bowkett made no comment on the potential bidder but City analysts mentioned the names of Swedish giant Electrolux and British firms Tomkins and Wassal Plc.
When asked whether the company was under any sort of pressure from institutional shareholders to change managment, Bowkett said, "we could still grow without any change in management".
He said the company faced no definite timeframe to decide on the possible offer.
Analysts covering the company said it would attract a price tag of 175 to 200 pence a share, valuing the company at 300 to 365 million stg, if the bid offer was launched.
